name: Julian
role: Roman emperor from 361 to 363, Neoplatonic philosopher
contribution: Caesar of the Western Roman Empire from 355 to 360 and Roman emperor from 361 to 363, as well as a notable philosopher and author in Greek.
legacy: This person was the last non-Christian ruler of the Roman Empire, and he believed it necessary to restore the Empire's ancient Roman values and traditions in order to save it from dissolution.

checks.lead: Julian (Latin: Flavius Claudius Julianus; Ancient Greek: Ἰουλιανός Ioulianos; 331 – 26 June 363) was Caesar of the Western Roman Empire from 355 to 360 and Roman emperor from 361 to 363, as well as a notable philosopher and author in Greek. His public conversion from Christianity to paganism and promotion of Neoplatonic form of Hellenism caused him to be remembered as Julian the Apostate in the Christian tradition.
